evidence.note: Strong upfront test-suite reconnaissance including examining wacc's feature-ordered chapter structure (1-18, struct chapters) — shows awareness that features are dependency-ordered, but is used for orientation rather than to build an explicit sequenced milestone plan.
Writes the entire compiler pipeline (token, types, preprocess, parse, codegen) in one push — the 'attempt the whole language at once' pattern rather than staged, per-feature milestones.
Some minimal staging: tests the simplest program, then more programs, then immediately runs the full 780-test suite — a coarse 'get simplest working' step but no layered feature progression.

The bulk of the run is a failure-driven whack-a-mole loop against the full suite (arbitrary failing tests across gcc-torture/c-testsuite/wacc), with per-suite failure counts (steps 90,128,615,647) but no named feature milestone, required pipeline change, or certifying test subset per milestone.
TodoWrite used periodically as a rough feature/task list, but sporadic and not tied to dependency ordering or per-milestone done-signals.

reasoning: The agent had a rough feature list (todos) and did solid test-structure recon plus a simplest-first check, which lifts it above anchor 0, and it tracks progress at the coarse per-suite level. But it wrote the whole pipeline at once and then worked failure-to-failure against the full 780-test suite rather than layering features in dependency-ordered milestones with per-milestone certifying tests, so it falls short of anchor 5. This places it at a 4 — between 'rough mental list, no explicit dependency sequencing' (3) and genuine staged progress-checking (5).
